text.p: Troubled One Holding Plc said on Friday its financial advisor had proposed a restructuring plan for the company which last month failed to meet payments on two bills of exchange worth $13.5 million.

The company outlined brief details of the restructuring plan in a statement to the Stock Exchange of Thailand. It said it would set up a steering committee made up of representatives of secured and unsecured lenders including the holders of One Holding's debenture and convertible debentures.
The company also plans to decrease its size of assets involving the investment and real estate business.
The SET, which had halted trade in One Holding shares in the morning session, said on Friday that dealings could resume in the afternoon since the company has issued a statement on the restructuring.
The share price closed at 2.60 baht on Thursday.
One Holding shares resumed trading on March 31 after a period of suspension as the company struggled with more than 7.0 billion baht ($269 million) in debt and defaulted on the bills of exchange.

It is the investment arm of Finance One Plc -- once Thailand's largest finance firm. One Holding's problems became public after Finance One had to merge with Thai lender Thai Danu Bank Plc to see off its own liquidity woes.
One Holding said it would focus on its original rubber business after it decreased its assets in investment and real estate.
The ailing company said its restructuring plan was aimed at allowing it to keep its status as a listed company.
"Once ONE has completed its restructuring plan which might require a time to take action... ONE will propose the long term business plan," the company said. It will then be presented to shareholders.
The company expects it will take up to seven months to set up a steering committee and decrease the size of its assets.
One Holding will call a meeting for debenture holders in mid-May to discuss the restructuring plan.
